title: Add the unguarded stdout-encoding detector (the cp1252 class)
intent: Promote the cp1252 defect class to a detector: flag CLI entry modules that write non-ASCII to stdout/stderr with no UTF-8 guard, which fails on Windows when the stream is piped, redirected or captured. Three witnessed instances motivated it (CAM-Assist-Blueprint arrow, code-audit's own __main__.py, the AGENTS.md scaffolder --dry-run of MAINT-DEFER-015).

scope.out_of_scope_notes: The instance fixes are not in this patch: code-audit's own __main__.py guard is fix/utf8-stdout-cp1252 (unmerged), and the scaffolder guard (MAINT-DEFER-015) belongs to the scaffolder's repo. The 11 high-tier findings this detector raises on this repo's scripts/ are left as findings, not fixed here. Detector B (hollow_guarantee) is already merged as PR #29 and Detector C (coverage drift) is a separate branch after triage.

what_changed: New analyzer analyzers/unguarded_stdout_encoding.py (1.0.0, advisory, severity LOW): one finding per CLI entry module whose unguarded stdout/stderr receives non-ASCII text; high tier when a literal reaches the sink within two local bindings, low tier when an untraceable value is printed and the module holds non-ASCII constants

Each finding records its failure modes, verified on Windows before being encoded: encode_crash (stdout, character outside cp1252), escaped_output (stderr, backslashreplace), undecodable_bytes (cp1252-encodable character such as an em-dash, unreadable to a UTF-8 reader)

Registered AnalyzerType.UNGUARDED_STDOUT_ENCODING and the analyzer in api._DEFAULT_ANALYZERS; refreshed logic, confidence_policy and confidence_golden manifests on Python 3.11 (closure-only change, no scoring change, no version bump)

30 tests: born-from acceptance for all three instances each paired with a guarded twin that must stay silent, plus controls, guard forms, entry detection, trace bounds and the two false-positive classes found while dogfooding
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: No existing analyzer looks at stream encoding. context_pinned_hash models implicit-context axes, but each axis is scoped to a value reaching a hash, and stdout is not a hash sink, so adding this there would have broken that analyzer's scoping (rail 7). The instance fixes each close one occurrence; this detector finds the class, including 11 latent occurrences in this repo's own scripts.

commands_run: py -3.11 -m pytest -o addopts="" -q (full suite, collect-all, CI=true, PYTHONPATH pinned to the worktree)
mutation check: detector disabled / guard recognition disabled / low tier disabled, each run against the test file
dogfood: analyzer over this repo, tests/fixtures/repos/*, luthiers-toolbox scripts+services, the canonical scaffolder, and the fix/utf8-stdout-cp1252 __main__.py
Windows subprocess reproduction of each failure mode with PYTHONIOENCODING/PYTHONUTF8 unset
test_results: Full suite (collect-all, CI=true, CONFIDENCE_ENTRYPOINTS as in pytest.yml): 1246 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed; the first run omitted CONFIDENCE_ENTRYPOINTS and its 3 env-contract failures pass once it is set
Clean origin/main baseline for comparison: 1214 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed (+30 = the new tests; 2 fewer skips = CI-only gates that run under CI=true)
Mutation check: disabling the detector fails 16 tests, disabling guard recognition fails the 5 guard tests, disabling the low tier fails the 5 low-tier tests
Manifests refreshed on Python 3.11 after the last source edit; version-bump and analyzer-registry contracts pass
verification.notes: Dogfood: fires high on code-audit's own main-branch __main__.py and is silent on the fix-branch version (loop-form reconfigure guard); fires high on the canonical scaffolder with U+2500 reported as an untraced encode-crash character; 0 findings on all 16 fixture repos (goldens stable). Two false-positive classes were found dogfooding and fixed with regression tests: a module docstring counted because the module read obj.__doc__ (deployment.py), and print(json.dumps(...)) whose default ensure_ascii=True output is pure ASCII. CI collection: tests/test_unguarded_stdout_encoding_analyzer.py is collected by the Pytest workflow's plain `python -m pytest -q` over testpaths=["tests"]; no pin needed.
